title: Jallianwala Bagh - A Place That Echoes India’s Freedom Struggle
content:
Jallianwala Bagh, Amritsar

Jallianwala Bagh is a historic memorial in Amritsar that marks the tragic massacre of 1919. Located close to the Golden Temple, Punjab it offers a powerful glimpse into India’s independence struggle through bullet-marked walls, Martyrs’ Well, Amar Jyoti, and peaceful gardens - making it a must-visit spot for tourists seeking history and reflection.

Why Is Jallianwala Bagh Important in History

The Jallianwala Bagh Massacre occurred on 13 April 1919 in Amritsar, when General Dyer ordered soldiers to fire on a large, unarmed crowd trapped inside the garden. People had gathered for a peaceful meeting and to protest the Rowlatt Act, as well as to celebrate Baisakhi. Without giving any warning, the troops fired continuously, killing hundreds and injuring thousands. The massacre shocked the entire country and revealed the brutality of British rule. It caused widespread anger, grief, and protests across India. This event became a major turning point in the freedom struggle and pushed Indians towards demanding complete independence from British rule.

What to Experience at Jallianwala Bagh ?

  • Martyrs’ Well - A protected memorial where hundreds jumped to escape the firing - a strong testament to survival and sacrifice.
  •  Bullet Marks on Walls - You can still see real bullet holes preserved on the brick walls - chilling evidence of the ruthless attack.
  • Amar Jyoti (Eternal Flame) - A flame that keeps burning in honor of those who lost their lives.
  •  Memorial Gallery - Displays photographs, documents & a short audio-visual history of the tragic event.
  •  Peaceful Gardens - Well-maintained lawns and pathways allow visitors to reflect in silence.

Best Time to Visit

  • Morning to sunset
  • Prefer winter and pleasant seasons for a comfortable experience

Tips for Travelers

  • Wear comfortable shoes as you will walk inside the memorial.
  • Maintain silence and respect - it is a place of remembrance.
  • Read history boards to understand the event better.
  • Plan your visit along with the Golden Temple (walking distance).
  • Visit early morning or evening to avoid crowd and heat.
  • Keep your mobile and wallet safe in the busy market outside.

Visiting Information

 Entry Fee: Free for all visitors
Timings: 6:30 AM to 7:30 PM (may vary slightly by season)
 Location: Very close to the Golden Temple, Amritsar, Punjab

-Jallianwala Bagh is a place that connects your heart with India’s history. Every corner here narrates a story of courage and sacrifice — making it a must-visit destination for anyone traveling to Amritsar.

Located near the Golden Temple, this historic memorial attracts millions of visitors who come to pay tribute to the lives lost in the tragic massacre of 1919. The calm atmosphere here silently tells the unforgettable story of bravery, pain, and sacrifice.
